annotations.text:
The whole home, for merchants who don't read much:
· money first — one big number, arrow up or down instead of percentages
· 'Do these now' tiles: a picture, a big count, one button
· one simple chart (Money each day) instead of four
· best sellers shown as photos
· order status = color chip with an icon (Send it / Paid / On the way)
· all numbers are sample values

Built for merchants who don't read much:
· pictures first — every step is an icon tile
· labels stay under 8 words
· exactly ONE loud tile (Do this now); the rest wait quietly
· progress you can see: ring + 5 segments, no reading needed
· done = green tile with a tick, crossed out on phone
· when all 5 are done the card celebrates once, then leaves

The setup strip, rethought:
· LEAD: a journey tracker — the order-tracking picture merchants already know. Done = filled tick, next = ringed with the only button, later = grey. Progress is spatial, no dead space.
· ALTERNATE: today's layout kept, but the next step becomes a tinted stat-card-style panel (matches the new money cards).
· All-clear card picks up the gradient icon chip.
· Phone: the tracker turns vertical, like package tracking.

Three more, each a different bet:
· SPOTLIGHT — only the next step exists, huge. Zero reading, zero clutter. Trade-off: the other steps are invisible.
· MARKET ROAD — a winding path to your shop, like a game map. Most memorable, most motivating. Trade-off: tallest, and playful may not fit every merchant.
· SLIM BAR — five dots and one button on a single line. Smallest possible footprint. Trade-off: least visual, small touch targets on phone.
